no pop-in, edge coverage or full-speed rendering. Extend projection/fog/track
range only in a separate traced experiment; do not disable native culling or
force index zero.


## ps2/MACOS
# macOS (Apple Silicon) port — status


:::note Source and evidence
PS2 implementation notes. Preserve each claim’s original evidence limits. CPU tests, static disassembly, proposals and live gameplay validation are different evidence levels. Consult [current Battle recovery](/ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY) for corrections and current status.

Source: `docs/MACOS.md` in `eod-recomp`. Repository HEAD: `67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7`. Working-copy modifications: `no`. Source SHA-256: `98e02311ce43b10d8dd853ff54249129ed6386bf874b0416a961ad02b08fb915`. Imported 2026-10-19. Addresses belong only to the platform/revision identified in the source; do not transfer Xbox addresses to PS2.
:::


> Current acceptance and branch map: [DEVELOPER_HANDOFF.md](DEVELOPER_HANDOFF.md).
> Historical speed samples below describe their specific builds/scenes. They do
> not establish current full-game 1:1 accuracy or full-speed heavy multiplayer.
> Current goal is native 1x/4:3 with no frame skipping before enhancements.

Branch `main` of catsandsoup/eod-recomp. Native arm64 build of the same
recompiled game code; no emulator, no Rosetta.

## Building

```sh
brew install cmake ninja libusb molten-vk vulkan-loader vulkan-headers
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install rabbitizer
cp "<your disc folder>/SLUS_209.10" .          # NTSC-U v1.00, never committed
.venv/bin/python tools/analyze.py && .venv/bin/python tools/recomp.py && .venv/bin/python tools/vurecomp.py
cmake -S . -B build-mac -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DPython3_EXECUTABLE=$PWD/.venv/bin/python
ninja -C build-mac
./build-mac/eod --data "<your disc folder>"     # folder with SLUS_209.10, SYSTEM.CNF, DATA/
```

Headless, muted test run: `EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1 ./build-mac/eod --headless --data ... --frames N --screenshot-every 300 --screenshot-dir out`.

## What works (verified 2026-10-16, M2 Pro, headless)

- Boot, intro movies, title screen, main menu, Action > Race > Multi.
- **2-player split screen race** with two independent pads:
  `tools/test_2p_race.sh "<disc folder>"` drives both ports with scripted
  pads and writes a contact sheet where each viewport reacts only to its own
  player's throttle (GOALS §0 verification without physical pads).
- Game logic runs at full speed (59.9 game frames/s in a 2P race).

## What changed for macOS

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| SIMD | `runtime/include/sse_compat.h`: the SSE2 intrinsics the VU/GS code uses, on NEON, with x86 results kept (cvttps out of range → 0x80000000; MXCSR DAZ/FTZ → FPCR.FZ). |
| Floats | `-ffp-contract=off` on arm64 so no FMA fusing: results match the x86 build. |
| Fibers | Direct arm64 register switch instead of ucontext (deprecated on macOS; swapcontext makes a syscall per switch). |
| Platform | `runtime/platform/sdl3/platform_sdl3.cpp`: window (SDL renderer, Metal), audio stream, keyboard + hot-plugged controllers on two player ports, analog triggers → L2/R2 pressure, rumble. |
| Input ports | Automatic (`KeyboardPort=-1`, or `EOD_KEYBOARD_PORT=auto`) assigns the first pad to P1 and then the keyboard to P2; a second pad takes P2. Keyboard alone starts on P1. Existing connected pads keep their ports on hot-plug; known reconnects restore free remembered slots. Explicit INI ports 0 (off), 1, 2 retain legacy behavior; environment ports are `none`, 1, 2. Saved settings are preserved. |
| Test input | `EOD_PAD_SCRIPT` (port 1) and `EOD_PAD_SCRIPT1` (port 2), optional left stick per entry: `frame:buttons:lx:ly`. |
| Threads | EE, GS, raster and offload threads ask for user-interactive QoS (P-cores). `EOD_GS_RASTER=n` is no longer capped at 4 when given explicitly. |

## Remaining validation

1. Visible resize/fullscreen and native first-run/settings dialogs need an
   interactive check; automation stays headless. High-refresh work is deferred.
2. Physical Rock Candy controller verification: bundled SDL/libusb and virtual
   tests pass, but no physical pad was connected during takeover. Original
   pressure mappings also need a usable modern throttle/brake layout.
3. Career save/resume and every event type need actual journey verification.
   Packet-level memory-card persistence tests pass; these alone do not establish
   that the game saves and resumes a career correctly.
4. Intro playback still needs fidelity/performance work. A bounded 8-second
   Apple Silicon CPU sample during `logos.pss` found the translated bitstream
   consume/refill helper `0039AFB0` at about 35% of main-thread self samples,
   with peek/consume wrapper `0039B048` at about 13%. Native IPU IDCT was below
   1% of self samples. This points to translated bitstream parsing as the first
   optimization target for that sampled segment; it does not establish the
   bottleneck for every movie or justify changing playback timing.

## Controllers and Rock Candy Xbox 360 wired pads

On macOS `EOD_BUNDLED_SDL=ON` is the default. CMake downloads pinned SDL
3.4.18 with a SHA-256 check, builds it statically with HIDAPI and libusb,
and fails configuration if libusb support is missing. Install `libusb`
with Homebrew first. `-DEOD_BUNDLED_SDL=OFF` uses installed SDL3; its libusb
capability depends on that build (Homebrew SDL3 does not enable it).
The linked Homebrew `libusb-1.0.0.dylib` must be copied into the application
bundle and its install name rewritten by the app packaging step. SDL itself
needs no separate dylib in the bundled configuration.

Plug the pad in and run this diagnostic from the repository (no disc data,
window, or audio needed):

```sh
EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1 ./build-mac/eod --list-pads --watch 30
```

Expect `HIDAPI over libusb: built in`, a controller with PDP vendor `0e6f`
(or Microsoft `045e`), `driver HIDAPI`, `opened as gamepad: yes`, and its SDL
mapping. The watch prints button changes, sticks centered at 128, and L2/R2
trigger pressure from 0 to 255; it briefly rumbles each assigned pad.
Unplug/replug during the watch to check hot-plug. With the default keyboard
on P1, one pad is P2. For two pads in plug order, use:

```sh
EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1 EOD_KEYBOARD_PORT=none ./build-mac/eod --list-pads --watch 30
```

If no pad appears, check `system_profiler SPUSBDataType` for PDP `0x0e6f`,
try another USB port/cable, and quit applications that may hold the device.
A virtual joystick cannot verify USB access, a physical mapping, or motors.
`EOD_INPUT_LOG=1` also logs changes per player during a game run.

Xbox A/B/X/Y map to Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle; LB/RB to L1/R1;
LT/RT to L2/R2 analog pressure plus the digital bit above 30/255 travel.
Back, Start, stick clicks and d-pad retain their corresponding PS2 controls.
Both sticks use a dead zone and the full 0..255 range. These mappings expose
PS2 L2/R2 pressure; the game's selected control scheme determines the actual
throttle and brake bindings.

Native settings also expose an opt-in Modern controller layout, persisted as
`[Input] ControllerLayout=modern` (default `original`). After relaunch, RT feeds
Cross pressure and LT feeds Square pressure, which the game's classic schemes
read as analog gas/brake. It suppresses the triggers' L2/R2 actions to avoid
double actions. Face buttons/keyboard keep full pressure even when a partial
trigger is held. Virtual tests cover partial/released triggers and two-port
isolation; physical driving feel remains unverified.

Hardware-free checks (headless and muted):

```sh
cmake --build build-mac --target eod eod_input_test eod_pad_rpc_test
EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1 ctest --test-dir build-mac --output-on-failure
EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1 tools/test_2p_race.sh "$HOME/Library/Application Support/TDEODRecomp/disc"
```
## Personal Mac app

The app requires your own North American SLUS-20910 v1.00 disc. No game
files are bundled. Generate and build as above, then enable packaging:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-mac -G Ninja -DEOD_MAC_APP=ON
cmake --build build-mac -j3
```

The plain `build-mac/eod` remains available. The `eod_app` target creates
`~/Library/Application Support/TDEODRecomp/local-build/Eve of Destruction.app`
with its non-system dylib dependency closure, local rpaths, the TDEOD
app icon, and ad-hoc signature. `EOD_APP_OUTPUT` chooses another output
directory. Use a directory outside iCloud/FileProvider: Finder metadata can
invalidate code signing inside synced Documents folders. The minimum macOS
version in Info.plist is derived from the executable and bundled dependencies
(at least 13.0); local Homebrew builds may require the current OS.

First launch offers a native ISO or disc-folder picker. It verifies the exact
SLUS_209.10 size and CRC before copying SLUS_209.10, SYSTEM.CNF (if present),
and DATA into Application Support/TDEODRecomp/disc. Progress and friendly
errors appear in native windows. An existing valid disc skips the picker.
Imports stage separately, and failed/cancelled copies preserve the old disc.
The built-in ISO9660 reader supports plain ISO and raw Mode 1/2 BIN/CUE.

`eod.ini` and `memcard/` also live in Application Support/TDEODRecomp.
Press **F1** or **Cmd+,** during play for native settings: video size,
fullscreen, aspect, smoothing, frame skip, VSync, volume/audio, every keyboard
binding, keyboard port, vibration, renderer and internal resolution, plus
save/disc locations. Aspect ratio and camera projection, renderer, internal resolution, VSync, audio
enable, frame skip, keyboard port and file locations take effect on next launch. The software renderer has no internal
resolution scaling; Vulkan selection requires a build with that backend.

Automation must set `EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1` and pass `--headless`.
`--data DIR`/`EOD_DATA`, `--config FILE` and `EOD_APP_SUPPORT` override paths.
Missing data in headless mode returns an error without opening dialogs.

```sh
ctest --test-dir build-mac --output-on-failure
# Read-only source; import only to a scratch destination:
build-mac/disc_import_cli /path/game.iso /tmp/eod-test/disc 3368996 75BB93EE
EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1 "$HOME/Library/Application Support/TDEODRecomp/local-build/Eve of Destruction.app/Contents/MacOS/eod" --headless --data /tmp/eod-test/disc --frames 600
# Build a DMG locally; never upload or distribute:
tools/make_dmg.sh
```

Native dialogs are compile-verified only; automated tests never open visible
windows or play audio. The app and DMG are personal builds only.

## Vulkan GS backend

`--renderer vulkan` is the macOS default when Vulkan headers/loader and SDL3
are available at configure time. `--renderer software` remains available;
`-DEOD_VULKAN=OFF` builds the software-only port. If the loader cannot discover
MoltenVK, set `VK_DRIVER_FILES` (or `VK_ICD_FILENAMES`) to its ICD JSON, normally
`/opt/homebrew/etc/vulkan/icd.d/MoltenVK_icd.json` for a Homebrew CLI build.

The backend retains the D3D11 renderer's GS page ownership, texture cache and
shader logic. Vulkan 1.3 dynamic rendering, push descriptors, dual-source
blending and depth clamp are required. Two fence-owned command/upload slots
allow CPU/GPU overlap. Sparse page conversions are coalesced without covering
unowned holes. Readbacks synchronize transfer writes to host reads. Default
presentation is FIFO; disabling vsync uses immediate/mailbox when supported.
`RenderScale=0` selects an initial scale covering the window's pixel height
(1x offscreen); explicit values 1–6 override it. A 1964-pixel panel needs 5x.
`EOD_SCREENSHOT_SCALE=5` captures the 5x composition rather than a 1x screenshot.

Verified 2026-10-16 on M2 Pro, entirely headless and muted:

- Existing `work/race2p.gsd`, 509,709 primitives / **nine** game frames per replay:
  software with four workers 369.8 ms; warm Vulkan 1x 113.0 ms (12.56 ms/frame),
  Vulkan 5x 120.4 ms (13.38 ms/frame). These are renderer replay timings;
  they do not prove visible presentation cadence.
- At 1x, RGB mean absolute difference versus software is 1.641/255;
  95% of channel differences are at most 4. Images are close, not bit exact.
  The 5x raster downsampled to 1x differs more (MAE 6.956/255).
- 379 forced rendered-page readbacks pass. Invalid ICD discovery falls back
  to software headlessly. SPIR-V regeneration validates all ten modules.
- 5x replay plus a 3200×2240 screenshot peaks near 1.00 GB total memory
  footprint including GPU allocations (315 MB resident), with no swaps.
- Scripted two-player racing reaches approximately 59.9 game/drawn frames/s;
  transient asset-loading dips remain. Logs and screenshots are local work
  artifacts, not committed game data.

Repeat full-game comparisons with `EOD_TEST_RENDERER=vulkan` and optionally
`EOD_TEST_CONFIG=work/vulkan5.ini` when invoking `tools/test_2p_race.sh`.
For a replay, save each generated `.gsd.ppm` before running another renderer,
because the next run overwrites that filename. Shader sources can be rebuilt
with `python3 tools/build_vk_shaders.py` (glslang and spirv-tools required);
the normal build uses the checked-in SPIR-V arrays.

Vulkan app bundles also include `libMoltenVK.dylib` and
`Contents/Resources/vulkan/icd.d/MoltenVK_icd.json`. MoltenVK is loaded
indirectly, so packaging includes it explicitly rather than relying only on
linked dependencies. Set `EOD_MOLTENVK_LIBRARY` at packaging time for a custom
driver path. Bundled launches set Vulkan driver discovery and SDL's Vulkan
loader path relative to the executable before both replay and normal startup;
copying the app requires neither Homebrew nor an external ICD configuration.
Plain command-line builds preserve the caller's Vulkan environment.

Test a relocated signed Vulkan app with intentionally invalid external ICD
overrides and an otherwise isolated environment:

```sh
tools/test_app_vulkan.sh "/path/Eve of Destruction.app" /path/race2p.gsd /tmp/app-vulkan.log
```

The script stays headless/muted and fails if replay falls back to software.

### Refresh-grid presentation (optional driver support)

Experimental and **off by default** while 1:1 fidelity is the priority. With
`EOD_PRESENT_TIMING=1` and `VK_GOOGLE_display_timing` advertised, the presenter learns
its refresh phase from completed presentation feedback and requests future
images near a fixed refresh grid. A 120 Hz display normally uses two refreshes
per guest image. The original 59.94 Hz game clock remains unchanged: on an
exactly 120 Hz fixed-rate display an occasional extra refresh is mathematically
necessary; missed deadlines also re-anchor instead of accumulating latency.
The default `EOD_PRESENT_TIMING=0` keeps this path deferred. Missing/invalid timing data
keeps ordinary FIFO presentation. Swapchain/refresh changes reset the schedule,
and no-vsync/catch-up sends no future presentation deadline.

This adds no sleep, device lock, or GPU fence wait. It cannot prevent the Vulkan
swapchain/driver's existing acquire/present calls from blocking. Visible cadence,
ProMotion's actual chosen refresh rate and GPU deadline misses still require an
interactive measurement; headless runs cannot verify this window-only path.
`tools/test_present_timing.sh` checks the pure scheduling logic without a Vulkan
or SDL device, including 120 Hz jitter, 59.94 Hz, rate mismatch, stalls and resets.

The approach was identified in Road Trip's `schedulePresent()`/`waitForDrawable()`;
our implementation is original, using the public extension rather than copied
renderer code. Source references:

- [Vulkan presentation timestamps](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPresentTimeGOOGLE.html)
- [MoltenVK presentation implementation](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/blob/main/MoltenVK/MoltenVK/GPUObjects/MVKImage.mm)
- [Apple's matching host-time epoch](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/quartzcore/cacurrentmediatime())
- [Road Trip's refresh-grid prior art](https://github.com/silentsudin/PS2Recomp/blob/818f279be3f9cdecaa9c7b4a3a7cbe8fe44fd6e4/ps2xRuntime/src/lib/gs/gs_pgs_presenter.cpp)

## Audio fidelity check

User volume is applied once by the shared SPU2 mixer. The SDL output stream
uses unity gain (or zero when disabled), so the Mac path no longer attenuates
50% volume twice. `audio_volume_offline` feeds constant planar stereo PCM
through the actual SPU2 AutoDMA/mixer and an unbound SDL stream, retrieves the
samples into memory, and checks 100%/50%/0% amplitudes of 11998/5999/0. It never
opens an audio device, window, or plays sound.

This fixes an output-level regression, not the whole PS2 sound model. The
current voice resampler is linear; noise/pitch-modulation and reverb fields
are stored but are not implemented in the mixing loop. Audio is driven from
wall-clock time, with a 100 ms catch-up limit and a 200 ms output queue cap.
Those approximations still require original-hardware or trusted-reference
comparison before describing audio or FMV synchronization as 1:1.

## Original-scale GS fidelity checks

Procedural 64×64 replays now exercise generated GS register packets without disc
assets or game code. `GSPixelArithmetic` and `VulkanGSPixels` are CTest checks
when Vulkan and testing are enabled. They demonstrate and guard these fixes:

- Gouraud RGBA truncation: an interior pixel formerly `(11,21,32)` is now
  `(10,21,31)`, matching the GS interpolation rule used by paraLLEl-GS.
- Linear UV precision: two interpolated coordinates in one 1/16-texel bucket
  formerly sampled 104 versus 96; both now sample 96.
- Fog interpolation: source and fog colour both 128 with F=255 formerly became
  127 in both software and Vulkan. Rounded interpolation about FogCol now
  preserves 128. The arithmetic test covers every constant colour/coefficient.

The original software-captured two-player fixture improves from RGB MAE
1.641 to 1.499/255 (95th-percentile channel difference 4→3). This is comparison
against our software renderer, not proof of exact PS2 output. In particular,
a generated blended rectangle exposes an interior `(15,29,45)` Vulkan result
where GS integer arithmetic gives `(14,28,44)`: fixed-function UNORM blending
still rounds. Large residual differences also remain around detailed geometry.
No complete 1:1 fidelity claim is justified yet; accurate GS/original-hardware
comparison is still needed. Filter-output rounding is deliberately not changed
merely to reduce software image error.

Hardware captures now flush pending GPU batches and read owned GS pages back
before serializing initial VRAM. Older captures taken from live Vulkan may
contain stale initial VRAM; software-captured fixtures avoid that limitation.
Replay state layout is unchanged and shared with the procedural generator.

Primary implementation evidence: [paraLLEl-GS interpolants, UV snapping and
fog counterexample](https://github.com/silentsudin/parallel-gs/blob/60e6cacead2dece90c4d85ebb5ae750d4aace143/gs/shaders/ubershader.comp).

## Movie bitstream helper optimization

The hot `0039AFB0` consume/refill helper has a native fast path for direct-RAM
reader state and either a disjoint RAM ring or the game's linear-input
`end=0xFFFFFFFF` sentinel. The sentinel path checks the exact next 1–8 bytes
against RAM bounds and state overlap. Unusual layouts, aliases and malformed
counts use the original generated function. Guest low/high register halves,
state stores and original interrupt safe points are preserved; after an
interrupt, a literal continuation uses ordinary guest memory accessors.

Regenerate after the HLE registry change, then build and run the differential
check (the reference is extracted locally into the ignored build directory):

```sh
.venv/bin/python tools/recomp.py
cmake -S . -B build-mac -G Ninja
cmake --build build-mac -j3
ctest --test-dir build-mac --output-on-failure
# Optional real movie bytes, read only; no fixture is saved:
EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1 build-mac/movie_bits_test "/path/disc/DATA/VIDEO/LOGOS.PSS"
```

The 12,000-case test compares the entire EE state, RAM and interrupt-boundary
snapshots against generated code, including ring wrap, linear sentinel,
64-bit shifts, overlapping inputs, aliases, pending interrupts and handler
mutations. A mixed-request 2-million-call microbenchmark measured roughly
1.7x improvement locally. Matched 8-second intro CPU samples reduced the
helper's self-sample share from about 34% to 21%, including wrapper overhead;
5- and 10-second screen captures were byte-identical. This is a bounded helper
cost improvement, not a proof of movie FPS, startup latency or full fidelity.

The existing `game`/`drawn` FPS counters use a render-buffer-switch heuristic.
Movies updating a fixed display buffer need not increment those counters, so
those numbers must not be reported as decoded movie frame rates.

## Display aspect and explicit output captures

Native settings support 4:3, 16:9, 16:10 and Stretch. Aspect changes are saved
for the next launch so composition and camera projection change together.
The default remains 4:3. Window width/height are macOS logical points; a
Retina drawable can contain more physical pixels. Internal scale 6 renders
640×448 GS content at 3840×2688; it does not force a physical monitor into a
3840×2160 or 3840×2400 output mode.

Live presentation and explicit output captures share the same centered aspect
rectangle. For example, 16:10 fills 3840×2400; on a 3024×1964 drawable it uses
3024×1890 with 37-pixel top/bottom bars. This preserves a 16:10 rectangle rather
than stretching into the extra display area.

For developer verification, set **both** output dimensions in physical pixels:

```sh
EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1 EOD_SCREENSHOT_WIDTH=3840 EOD_SCREENSHOT_HEIGHT=2400 \
  build-mac/eod --headless --config /path/16-10.ini --renderer vulkan \
  --gs-replay /path/race2p.gsd --repeat 1
```

Use `[Video] AspectRatio=16:10` and `RenderScale=6` in that test config. The
capture includes the aspect rectangle and black letterboxing at exactly the
requested size. Each dimension must be 1–8192. Without these variables, the
existing native-GS screenshot/`EOD_SCREENSHOT_SCALE` behavior is unchanged.
Replay display configuration is initialized without opening SDL devices.
CPU tests cover 4K/MBP rectangles, capture-size validation, startup aspect
persistence after a later settings save, and 16:10 config round-trip. Actual
GPU composition validation belongs to the combined camera/display build.


### Keyboard racing preset

The default **Racing (WASD + arrows)** keyboard layout uses WASD or arrow keys
for menus; Enter accepts and Escape goes back. In races, W/Up accelerates,
S/Down or **Space brakes**, A/D or Left/Right steers, and Escape pauses.
Enter starts the title screen and has no driving action. Release held keys
when changing screens. Opposite steering keys cancel to center.
Select **Original (PS2 keys)** to use the per-button key bindings instead;
`[Input] KeyboardLayout=racing|original` persists this choice. Gamepad layout
is a separate setting. Target-state evidence is in [KEYBOARD_CONTEXT.md](KEYBOARD_CONTEXT.md).

Explicit wide aspect settings preserve original menu/title/movie art at 4:3.
The native camera and display mode switch together only for the actual race
loop; pause overlays inside that loop retain its aspect. Per-frame presentation
is carried in GS queue order, including output captures. Matched 4:3/wide 3D
scene comparisons are still required to validate horizontal field of view and
object proportions. On macOS the GS queue defaults to at most two outstanding
vblanks for lower input latency; `EOD_GS_LAG` remains a developer override.

## Optional detail presets

F1 Settings → Detail (next launch) offers Original (default), High and Maximum.
The INI setting is `[Video] Detail=original|high|maximum`. High scales positive
car LOD thresholds by3; Maximum keeps the highest native permitted loaded model
throughout the supported visible range and restores the one-player projection/
fog distance in two-player cameras. Restart after changing it. The legacy
`EOD_CAR_LOD_MULTIPLIER` environment value overrides the preset for experiments.
No user setting is automatically changed. See [DETAIL_PRESETS.md](DETAIL_PRESETS.md)
for tests, performance, comparison images and the limits of the tested scene.


## ps2/MANUAL_RECOVERY
# Human manual recovery


:::note Source and evidence
PS2 implementation notes. Preserve each claim’s original evidence limits. CPU tests, static disassembly, proposals and live gameplay validation are different evidence levels. Consult [current Battle recovery](/ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY) for corrections and current status.

Source: `docs/MANUAL_RECOVERY.md` in `eod-recomp`. Repository HEAD: `67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7`. Working-copy modifications: `no`. Source SHA-256: `1dc3bb47fd8feb8672e260f660f863c7008027161cc742fbd0eebe8d6b478531`. Imported 2026-10-19. Addresses belong only to the platform/revision identified in the source; do not transfer Xbox addresses to PS2.
:::


## Player success

With `[Gameplay] ManualRecovery=1`, local humans may remain wrong-way,
off-track or upside-down beyond the native recovery countdown without that
countdown relocating them. Its warning disappears. SELECT remains available
under the native recovery eligibility rules. AI recovery and ordinary race
initialization/restart remain native. Default `0` preserves the original game.
This does not remove solid world boundaries or other out-of-world safety code.

## Situation and task

The owner requested removal of the “Get back in the race!” countdown, while
keeping manual SELECT and AI recovery. Hiding text alone would still teleport
the car; clearing its deadline would disable the direct SELECT recovery path.

## Action and native evidence

SLUS-209.10 function `001B8370` evaluates the native recovery conditions and
updates their timers. Its automatic-expiry branch calls `001B63E8` at return
address `001B8884`, gated by the word at `00485098`. The human wrapper disables
that word only during this native call and restores its exact value afterward.
It retains native detection/timers and native EE register side effects.

The participant is argument 1, its car is at +4, and its HUD stats are +0x40.
The stats warning flag +128 is participant +192; the deadline +132 is participant
+196. The original deadline is the PS2 float sum of timer +68 and +72. The
wrapper reproduces that same deadline when active, then clears only the warning.
Manual input `0018EA04` requires a positive deadline before calling `001B63E8`;
when ineligible, its existing `001DA3E0` event-manager path remains unchanged.

Only PCAR (`car+12 == 0x50434152`) local-player type `0x50` qualifies.
Constructor `001D92A8` creates these local-player cars; AI constructor
`001D92A0` uses type `0x51`. AI/remote/special cars, disabled settings and invalid
host-inspected pointers fall through to the original. No reset function, spawn,
restart, world resource or physics implementation is patched.

Reuse check: [RoadTripAdventure recomp overrides](https://github.com/silentsudin/RoadTripAdventure-recomp/blob/0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8/src/game/overrides.cpp)
was rechecked for this issue. Its native-wrapper approach fits; its game-specific
addresses and recovery ABI do not. This uses EOD's existing HLE wrap mechanism,
not an independent recovery implementation.

## Result and limits

CPU contract: a passthrough wrapper first failed “human expired countdown cannot
reset”; the implemented wrapper passes. Coverage includes native register effects,
default-off behavior, AI passthrough, exact global restoration, native SELECT
deadline, non-countdown modes, invalid pointers, and config save/load.

Live evidence and installation are recorded below after validation. Automated
runs isolate memory cards and use headless/muted mode. A controlled native
predicate test is not proof of physically driving every track, overturning every
car or traversing every out-of-world boundary.

Live controlled test (2026-10-17): two 7,500-vblank Dennison split-screen runs,
separate empty memory cards, native 1x rendering. Generated-code-only validation
fed the upside-down predicate from native race time 10–50 seconds, without
changing vehicle physics. The production wrapper and original timer/reset/input
functions executed. Human car indices 8/9 were both type 0x50; AI indices 0–7
were 0x51. A separate AI index-2 predicate attempt did not produce an AI reset,
so runtime AI recovery itself is not claimed tested.

- ManualRecovery=0: each human had four automatic reset calls at RA `001B8884`,
  and one SELECT reset at RA `0018EA04`. Both HUDs showed the countdown.
- ManualRecovery=1: zero automatic reset calls; each human still had one SELECT
  reset at `0018EA04`. All sampled HUD warning flags were zero. P2 retained
  deadline 18.013 at native time 45.7624 before its manual reset, proving manual
  eligibility survives beyond expiry. Both runs reached their bound and exited 0.
- Screenshots at frame 5100 confirm the visible warning in baseline and absence
  in both modified viewports. Positions differ between runs; this is a behavior
  comparison, not deterministic image parity.

Evidence (ignored): `work/recovery/injected-{off,on}/out.log`,
`frame_05100.png`, script `work/recovery/race.sh`. The instrumented generated
sources are not shipped; the production sources were restored before final build.
Remaining limit: no exhaustive physical upside-down/off-track drive across all
tracks, no runtime AI recovery event, no claim that independent hard-world safety
teleports are disabled. AI passthrough is covered by the CPU contract and unchanged
native call sites. Next decisive regression test is ordinary human exploration
with SELECT on each player's physical controller.

Production validation: all 48 CTest cases passed (15.95s), including
ManualRecovery. Full Release app build completed; strict deep codesign
verification passed. Neither generated validation predicate nor diagnostic log
strings remains in the restored generated files.

Live UI toggle: open Settings (F1 or Command-comma on Mac), change
“Manual recovery only”, and Save. It applies when gameplay resumes without a
restart. The Windows overlay exposes the same checkbox in its Gameplay tab;
it applies immediately, and Save settings persists it. Turning it off restores
native countdown recovery. The CPU regression exercises off/on changes in one
process. The Mac settings UI builds successfully; Windows UI interaction has not
been tested locally.


## ps2/MODDING_IDEAS
# Owner's mod ideas (2026-10-17, condensed from the owner's design doc)


:::note Source and evidence
PS2 implementation notes. Preserve each claim’s original evidence limits. CPU tests, static disassembly, proposals and live gameplay validation are different evidence levels. Consult [current Battle recovery](/ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY) for corrections and current status.

Source: `docs/MODDING_IDEAS.md` in `eod-recomp`. Repository HEAD: `67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7`. Working-copy modifications: `no`. Addresses belong only to the platform/revision identified in the source; do not transfer Xbox addresses to PS2.
:::


Priority set by owner: **LOD first, especially in split screen.**

## Engine upgrades
1. Infinite Junkyard: detached parts (bumpers, hoods, tires) never despawn (remove TTL, bigger debris pool); cars and debris always at full detail (LOD 0) at any distance.
2. Dynamic track perimeters: tire walls, hay bales, fence posts become physics objects; concrete barriers break above an impact threshold.
3. Eve's Diner Cannonball Run: remove event barriers/reset triggers, stitch hub world + tracks, point-to-point races through town and venues.
4. Destructible shortcuts: heavy cars break campaign barriers mid-race; AI uses the opened route.
5. Hub-world Infection: whole town at night, headlight-only lighting.

## Game modes (party/multiplayer)
Patient Zero (infection, Hearse horde), Trash Compactor (heavy rolling School Bus vs compacts in the Quarry), Gauntlet Sniper (stationary mortar player over the Figure-8), Ice Rink Sumo (zero-grip arena, push out of bounds), Smokey & the Bandit (cops vs robbers, 3 s pin = busted), The Sweeper (rotating buses, jump cheat), Ejector Seat Bowling (launch chassis for distance), Meat Grinder (ramp over oval infield into oncoming traffic), Arena Combat (crates give mortar/mine), Keanu's Revenge (towed trailers, last place explodes every 20 s), Pinball Derby (bouncy walls x2.5), Shackled Sprint (teams chained 30 ft apart), Red Light Green Light, Quarry Bowling (Ambulance vs parked Taxis), Relic Hunt (collect tokens, AI buses hunt you).

Note: many assume more players/cars than the game's 2P split screen and car limits; these need the engine work above first.

## Owner priority update — October 16, 2026

LOD, draw distance and correct widescreen/ultrawide culling are now a **high
priority workstream**, explicitly promoted by the owner from the otherwise
deferred mod list. Target very distant highest-available-detail rendering and
eliminate visible model/quality pop-in where the engine/assets permit. Support
scalable Maximum/Extreme settings for faster Macs and high-end 8K PCs, beyond
what the owner's M2 Pro can run at full speed. Retain a playable Mac preset.
DLSS is explicitly the very last priority. Preserve
original physics, AI and simulation timing; maintain a faithful baseline for
comparison. Other mods and 120 Hz remain deferred.

Do not equate disabling all culling with correct wide-aspect visibility. Trace
frustum construction, per-camera aspect, bounding-volume tests, distance/LOD
selection, scene submission and asset streaming separately. Correct edge
visibility while retaining valid visibility tests; measure costs per player in
split screen. Use reproducible camera sweeps, distant opponent/track objects,
wide-edge captures and frame-time/geometry/memory measurements. A dedicated
fresh specialist investigation is appropriate for this research/implementation stream.

Zero pop-in is an acceptance ambition, **not an established feasible guarantee**.
First establish whether highest-detail assets exist, remain resident, and can
be submitted beyond original engine limits. More internal render pixels alone
do not create higher-resolution textures or more detailed meshes. Document
engine bounds and any loading/streaming limits before promising removal.

The historical planning-only note below remains context for other mod ideas;
it does not override this newer LOD/culling priority.

> **Status: planning only.** Modding is parked until the macOS port of this PS2
> recompilation reaches 1:1 parity and passes the 2-player split-screen
> requirement (see `TDEOD RECOMP/GOALS.md` §0 and `docs/MODDING_IDEAS.md` there).
> Nothing here has been implemented. Every mod must be opt-in and must leave the
> default game unchanged.
>
> **Verified against the PS2 data on 2026-10-16.** First written from the owner's
> **Xbox** disc (`TDEOD RECOMP/game/`), then checked against the owner's **PS2**
> disc files (`SLUS_209.10` + `DATA/`, read in place from
> `~/Library/Application Support/TDEODRecomp/disc`; the ELF is byte-identical to
> the one in this repo). Format findings come from throwaway parsers in
> `/private/tmp/prior investigation-501/eodmod/` (Xbox) and `/private/tmp/prior investigation-501/eodmod-ps2/`
> (PS2, plus `xs.py`, a string/address cross-reference helper for the ELF).
> Nothing was extracted into a repo. Claims still unverified are marked
> **(guess)** or **(unverified)**.

## 0. Summary

**Main finding: almost all game content and rules are stored as data in a
key/value table format we can decode, and that data is the same on PS2 and
Xbox.** All 755 `VALT` tables (event rules, AI tuning, car physics, damage
bones, prop placement, arena bounds, camera FOVs, driver roster) are
semantically identical on both discs, and so are all `ILIN` racing/ghost lines
and the track collision files (`SOBL/SCOL/BSPT/BPPT`, byte-identical). Only
graphics (`TEX`, `MODL`, `GRAF`, UI images) and audio/video differ. The archive
format (`0TSR`, §2.1) is a slightly older version on PS2 (v6 vs v7) and its
checksums are now **solved**: they are a CRC32 found in the ELF, so repacking
is safe.

Three PS2-specific findings change the plan:
* **Widescreen is built into the PS2 game** (options menu "Widescreen (16:9)",
  a real Hor+ projection). With the port's `AspectRatio=16:9` it may already
  work; it needs a check, not a mod (§1.2).
* **PS2 textures are 4/8-bit palettized and GS-swizzled, at the same resolution
  as Xbox's DXT textures.** The Xbox disc is not a source of *higher-resolution*
  textures, only of full-colour ones (64% of PS2 textures have 16 colours) (§2.4).
* **PS2 meshes are pre-built VIF/VU1 packets** (`SPS4` parts), so new cars and
  tracks need a VIF packet writer. The Xbox meshes (`DNIS` parts, plain
  vertex/index arrays) are a clean source for that conversion: the part lists
  match one to one (§2.5).

Code changes are needed only for these things: raising vehicle caps, adding new
event rule types, more than 2 split-screen views, new rendering effects, and
frame interpolation.

**Engine lineage is confirmed. The closest sibling is NASCAR: Dirt to Daytona
(2002, PS2/GameCube), not Heat 2002.** Evidence is in §6.1.

| # | Idea | Feasibility (PS2-based port) | Rough effort* | Main prerequisite |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | **Mod overlay folder** (`mods/<name>/DATA/...` merged over `DATA/` in the virtual disc) | **High** | 1–2 days | none (`build_disc()` in `runtime/iop/stream.cpp`); names must be ISO 8.3 (§2.2) |
| F2 | `0TSR` archive unpack/repack tool | **High** (CRC solved) | 1–3 days | none; CRC = `f_00135FC8` (§2.1) |
| F3 | `VALT` ⇄ text decompiler/compiler (round-trip) | **High** | 3–5 days | F2 |
| G1 | Higher internal resolution | **Done** on D3D11 (1–6×); needs to be redone in the Mac renderer | part of the port | Mac GPU GS backend |
| G2 | Widescreen (true 16:9 field of view) | **High: already in the game** | 0.5–2 days (verify, optional auto-select) | test in-game option + `AspectRatio=16:9` (§1.2) |
| G3 | Texture replacement / HD pack (keyed at GS upload, names from the texture loader) | **Med-High** | 2–3 weeks | Mac GPU backend, dump tool, hook `f_00350F58` |
| G4 | Xbox textures in the PS2 port | **Med** (easy mapping, modest gain) | 1–3 weeks | G3 (true-colour path) or a PS2 `TEX` writer |
| G5 | New post effects (CRT filter, bloom, sharpening, AA) | **High** | days each | Mac GPU backend |

| T3 | In-game/standalone track editor | **Low** (as a full editor); **Med** as a "Blender plus exporter" pipeline | months | T2 |
| A1 | Re-tune AI (lookahead, skill, speed factors) | **High** | hours | F3 |
| A2 | Auto-generate AI racing lines (`.ild`) for new tracks | **Med** | 2–4 weeks | `.ild` layout (same on both platforms, §4) |
| A3 | Replace the AI | **Low** | months | deep code reverse engineering |
| MP1 | New multiplayer **variants** (existing rules, new parameters/props) | **High** | hours per mode | F1–F3 |
| MP2 | New multiplayer **rule types** (Reverse Only, Juggernaut, etc.) | **Med** (simple ones as HLE hooks) / **Low** (Chain Gang) | 1–4 weeks each | find player-input/damage functions in the ELF |
| MP3a | More than 20 vehicles | **Low** | months | the race setup holds exactly 20 car slots (§5.2) |
| MP3b | 3–4 player split screen | **Low** (input side is ready) | months | viewport/camera/HUD code for >2 views does not exist |
| N1 | NASCAR Heat (PC 2000) **car** import | **Med-Low** (after M3) | 1–2 months | M3 pipeline, re-rig damage bones |
| N2 | NASCAR Heat / Dirt to Daytona **track** import | **Low-Med** | 2–4 months for the first track | T2 + scale/AI lines |
| N3 | Physics value transplant (Heat `.val` to EoD `physics.val`) | **Med-High** | days | F3 (key names look shared) |

\*Effort is a rough single-developer estimate after parity is reached. It
assumes the existing recompilation tooling and gets cheaper with each repeat.

### 0.1 PS2 hook points found in this pass
Addresses are EE addresses in `SLUS_209.10` (view with `tools/dis.py -f <addr>`).
None of these are in `config/symbols.txt` yet; the names are descriptive guesses
from strings and code shape. HLE `wrap`/`replace` entries go in `config/hle.txt`.

| Address | What it is (evidence) | Mod use |
|---|---|---|
| `00135FC8` | Resource CRC32 (MSB-first, poly 0x04C11DB7, table at `003F2598`) | reproduce in the repacker (done in Python) |
| `0012FEA0` | Resource-set header check (cookie `0TSR`, version 6, header size 0x28, file size, header CRC) | none needed |
| `00130980` / `00130C30` / `00130170` | `load_resource_set`, entry extraction with CRC check, `check_all_resident_crcs` | debug logging of loaded sets |
| `00331708` | Path to ISO 8.3 name mangler (`EmptyTrack.trk` → `EMPTYT_1.TRK`) | naming rule for new files |
| `0033D4F8` | `StrmFindFile` (already wrapped) | log missing mod files |
| `00350F58` / `003545B8` | Texture load by name, then optional `<name>.tm0` high-detail variant | **G3/G4 name ↔ GS upload mapping** |
| `0034D328` | `SetDisplayMode(0 normal, 1 widescreen, 2 letterbox)`; saves option `display_type` | G2 |
| `0032EC58` | Boot-time "console is set to 16:9" query; `main` calls `SetDisplayMode(1)` if non-zero | G2: wrap to follow the port's `AspectRatio` |
| `0034E530` | Projection setup (near, far, FOV in radians; divides by the x-scale at `003DD658`); called with (1, 1000, 67.5°) from `002127B0` | FOV mods, G2 |
| `00212808` | Detail setup: option `draw_distance` (0–2) → factor at `00495D58`; also `detail_level` | draw-distance mod |
| `00137838` / `00137750` / `001377C0` | Options get-int / get / set (key + section id) | force any option |
| `00123B98` | Eve/contest loader (validates contests; chassis ≤ 7, trailer-race vehicles ≤ 20) | MP1/MP3 |
| `0020FD48` | `create_cars`: 20 slots × 0x78 bytes, count at slot base + 0x960 | MP3a |
| `00331FD0` | Pad init: loads `mtapman.irx` + `padman.irx`, opens up to 5 pad ports | MP3b input |
